subject: MSA security exhibit: proposed assurance schedule and redline questions
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthcore.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurements <procure@healthcore.com>
Date: 2026-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA security exhibit — initial questions on SOC 2 assertions and pen test window

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending the MSA & security exhibit draft earlier this week. We reviewed it with Infrastructure and Procurement and have a couple of clarifying asks before we move to legal redlines:  

1) SOC 2: can you confirm which control period the attestation will cover for the first 12 months post-go-live? We need a clear start/end for our compliance calendar.
2) Pen test language: the draft requires vendor-initiated penetration testing but is silent on whether HealthCore can request an additional scoped test and chargeback. Please clarify the escalation and timing.
3) Audit access: we need to understand the expected evidence cadence and whether sampling windows will be staggered (we prefer quarterly windows vs. a single annual block).

Can you propose an evidence schedule that maps to the SOC 2 period and includes an escalation path for urgent audit requests? Also attaching the spreadsheet with our preferred windows for reference.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Information Security
HealthCore Medical

[Attachment: healthcore_audit_windows.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthcore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA security exhibit — initial questions on SOC 2 assertions and pen test window

Hi Elena — appreciated, and good questions. High level answers here, with Karthik/Laura looped for legal/ops detail:  

- SOC 2 coverage: Redwood's attestation period will start from the Service Commencement Date (we typically align to go-live month). For this engagement we can commit the first 12-month attestation to cover the first full calendar quarter after go-live through the following quarter (i.e., a rolling 12-month period). If HealthCore needs fixed calendar-year coverage we can discuss carveouts.

- Pen tests: Redwood performs annual vendor-initiated tests and supports customer-triggered scoped tests. For customer-requested tests we ask for a 30-day notice and a scoping call; if the request is outside normal windows there may be a cost-recovery fee. Karthik, can you confirm the proposed contract language and an exception path for urgent requests?

- Evidence cadence: we can offer staggered quarterly evidence windows by control family (access controls, change management, incident response, etc.). That maps better to ops cycles than a single annual window. I'll propose a draft calendar attached.

Next steps: Karthik/Laura — could you prepare a redline that: 1) defines the attestation period, 2) updates pen-test clause to include 30-day notice + scoped test fee language, and 3) enumerates evidence cadence options (quarterly stagger, annual snapshot)? Elena — once we have that redline we can run it past your legal/procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposed_evidence_calendar_draft.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthcore.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA security exhibit — initial questions on SOC 2 assertions and pen test window

Marissa/Elena — thanks, looping in legal detail below and attaching a tracked redline (v1). Key points:  

1) Attestation period: proposed language — "Customer's SOC 2 attestation will cover a continuous 12-month period beginning on the Service Commencement Date; the parties may agree on a fixed calendar-year period in writing." This keeps standard practice but gives an option if HealthCore needs fixed-year coverage.

2) Pen testing: proposed clause — "Customer may request an additional scoped penetration test with thirty (30) days' prior written notice. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate such requests; if the requested test requires additional resources outside of Redwood's routine testing program, the Customer will be responsible for reasonable, documented cost recovery fees. In urgent situations where a Customer-requested test is required within less than thirty (30) days, the parties will meet to agree scope and timing; Redwood will not be obligated to comply without mutual written agreement."

3) Evidence cadence and sampling: propose a quarterly staggered evidence window by control family. Example schedule attached — quarter 1: identity & access; quarter 2: change mgmt & deployments; quarter 3: incident response & monitoring; quarter 4: backups & retention. For customers that prefer annual snapshots we will retain a playbook for a single-window approach.

4) Escalation & emergency audits: added a short escalation path to the exhibit — CS engagement lead -> Security Ops -> Legal -> Exec sponsor; required approvals and expected time-to-respond windows.

I'll attach redline and a lightweight ops SLA matrix for Customer review. Please confirm if any of this is a non-starter for HealthCore so I can iterate.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redline_security_exhibit_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthcore.com>

Cc: Procurements <procure@healthcore.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T13:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA security exhibit — initial questions on SOC 2 assertions and pen test window

Karthik/Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the concrete language. A few follow-ups from our security and procurement teams:  

- The attestation language above is acceptable provided Redwood confirms the first attestation will be delivered within 120 days of the completion of the first covered quarter (HealthCore's internal audit calendar requires a delivery deadline). Can you add a delivery timeline?
- Regarding pen tests: HealthCore's policy requires the customer-requested scoped test to have guaranteed root-cause follow-up support (timeline to remediate critical findings). Can Redwood add a remediation SLA or at least a joint remediation plan commitment for critical severities?
- Evidence windows: quarterly by control family is preferable. Can we get an example week-of windows (e.g., week 2 of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct) to put into our procurement schedule?

If you can incorporate the delivery timeline and remediation commitments we should be able to proceed to a final redline and procurement approval.

Thanks,
Elena

Elena — hi, Laura from Ops here. Quick update to address the operational asks so legal can finalize language:  

1) SOC 2 report delivery: Redwood confirms we will deliver the SOC 2 report within 120 days after the end of the covered quarter. I'll add the exact clause: "Redwood will provide Customer with an executive summary of the SOC 2 report within ninety (90) days and the full report within one hundred twenty (120) days following the end of the relevant covered quarter."

2) Remediation for critical pen-test findings: Redwood will commit to a joint remediation plan for Critical severity findings with an initial mitigation plan within 10 business days and a remediation target of 45 calendar days unless otherwise agreed for infrastructure-level fixes. We'll document exceptions where third-party dependencies apply.

3) Evidence windows: proposed default weeks are Week 2 of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct (i.e., the second Monday of each quarter). We can also support a customer-specified week with 30 days' notice. We'll add the sample calendar as an attachment.

I added these items to redline v2 and attached the calendar and a small ops SLA matrix. If these are good, Karthik — can you fold the ops wording into the exhibit and we'll circulate a final tracked redline for signature?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
